summary: LLM token prices fell roughly 80% between 2025 and 2026, yet enterprise API bills continue to explode past $8.4 billion annually as usage scales faster than prices drop. A combined optimization strategy spanning caching, model routing, prompt compression, and output control routinely cuts total inference spend by 60-80% with no loss in output quality. The highest-leverage, lowest-risk lever remains prompt caching, which every major provider now ships natively and which can reduce input costs on repeated prefixes by up to 90%.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Provider-Native)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated, static prompt prefix (system prompts, RAG knowledge bases, few-shot examples) so repeated requests skip recomputation and are billed at a steep discount. The saving is structural with zero change to model output. Key engineering work is ordering the prompt so the static portion stays byte-identical across calls.
techniques.example: Place your 20,000-token system prompt and RAG context at the start of every request and append only the user's variable query at the end; Anthropic and OpenAI then cache the static prefix, dropping its cost by up to 90% on subsequent calls within the cache TTL.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches full responses keyed by the semantic meaning (embedding similarity) of a query rather than exact text match, so paraphrased or near-identical questions return a stored answer without hitting the model at all. Complementary to prompt caching: prompt caching cheapens tokens that always appear, semantic caching eliminates entire calls.
techniques.savings: 30-50% fewer total calls (typical 45% cache hit rate)
techniques.example: Route all incoming chatbot queries through a Redis semantic cache; when 'How do I reset my password?' and 'password reset help' resolve to the same embedding neighborhood, serve the cached answer and skip the LLM entirely.

techniques.name: Model Routing (Tiered Cascade)
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, sending simple or high-volume queries to budget-tier models and reserving frontier models for genuinely hard tasks. Flagship models cost 4-16x more than budget tiers for identical token counts, so routing attacks the largest single cost multiplier.
techniques.example: A support chatbot handling 1M monthly conversations (500 input / 200 output tokens) costs $3,250/mo on a flagship model at $2.50/$10.00; routing 70% of easy queries to a $0.15/$0.60 budget model drops the same workload toward $195 for that tier, a 16x saving on routed traffic.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of input tokens by removing redundancy, trimming verbose instructions, pruning low-value context, and using compression models (e.g. LLMLingua) to condense prompts while preserving meaning. Attacks the input side of the token bill directly.
techniques.example: Run a 4,000-token RAG context through LLMLingua to compress it to ~2,400 tokens before sending, preserving the answer quality while cutting 40% of input cost on every call.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Constrains the number of output tokens the model generates, since output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens on flagship models. Achieved via max_tokens limits, explicit instructions to be concise, and structured/JSON output schemas that eliminate filler prose.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct 'Respond in at most 3 bullet points' for a classification task, cutting output tokens by half and directly removing the most expensive tokens from the bill.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through provider batch APIs that process asynchronously (typically within 24 hours) at a roughly 50% discount versus synchronous calls. Ideal for offline workloads like evaluations, bulk summarization, and data enrichment.
techniques.example: Submit a nightly job of 100,000 document summarizations via OpenAI's Batch API instead of real-time calls to halve the token cost for that workload.

techniques.name: Monitoring & Cost Observability
techniques.description: Instruments every request with per-call token and cost logging, tagged by feature, user, and model, so you can find waste, detect prompt bloat, and measure the impact of other optimizations. Monitoring doesn't save tokens directly but is prerequisite to every other lever.
techniques.example: Add a Helicone proxy header to all calls and discover that one legacy feature consumes 40% of spend on an oversized prompt, then fix just that endpoint.

techniques.name: KV Cache Management (Self-Hosted Inference)
techniques.description: At the infrastructure level, tuning the inference server's internal key-value cache (prefix sharing, paged attention, cache eviction policy) maximizes GPU throughput and reduces redundant recomputation for self-hosted or open-source deployments.
techniques.example: Enable automatic prefix caching in vLLM so many concurrent requests sharing a long system prompt reuse the same KV tensors, raising throughput without extra GPUs.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity, reducing repeated API calls for similar queries.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, Zilliz-maintained); self-hosted infra costs only

tools.name: Redis / Redis LangCache
tools.description: In-memory data store offering vector search for semantic caching of LLM responses and fast exact-match prompt caching; LangCache is Redis's managed semantic caching service.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, LangCache usage-based enterprise pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Open-source unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers offering model routing, fallback, load balancing, caching, and per-key spend tracking through a single OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, audit logs, and support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and cost monitoring proxy that logs tokens, cost, and latency per request, with built-in caching, rate limiting, and prompt analytics.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier up to 10k requests/mo; Pro from $20/mo, enterprise custom

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source LLM engineering platform for tracing, cost monitoring, prompt management, and evaluation across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free self-hosted & cloud hobby tier; Cloud Pro from $59/mo

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: High-performance LLM gateway providing semantic caching, model routing, and failover; commonly paired with provider-native prompt caching to cut input tokens by an order of magnitude.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS core; managed/enterprise tiers custom-priced

tools.name: LangChain / LangSmith
tools.description: LangChain framework provides built-in LLM response caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite) and routing primitives; LangSmith adds tracing and cost observability.
tools.pricing_paid: LangChain free OSS; LangSmith free developer tier, Plus from $39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt compression toolkit that condenses prompts and context using a small language model while preserving task performance, cutting input tokens.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, MIT); compute cost only

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API marketplace routing requests across hundreds of models with transparent per-token pricing, automatic fallback, and cost-based routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Free to use; pay per-token at provider rates plus small markup

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: Open-source high-throughput inference engine with PagedAttention and automatic prefix (KV) caching for efficient self-hosted serving of open-source models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, Apache 2.0); GPU infrastructure cost only

quick_wins: Enable provider-native prompt caching and reorder prompts so all static content (system prompt, RAG context, few-shot examples) comes first — up to 90% off repeated input tokens with no quality loss.
Set sensible max_tokens limits and instruct the model to be concise, since output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens.
Route high-volume simple queries to a budget-tier model and reserve the frontier model for hard tasks — often a 16x cost difference for identical token counts.
Add a semantic cache (Redis or GPTCache) in front of the model to serve paraphrased repeat questions without any API call — typical 40-45% hit rates.
Drop in an observability proxy like Helicone or Langfuse to tag spend per feature/model and immediately surface prompt bloat and wasteful endpoints.
